name: Tooheys Forest
subtitle: South Brisbane · Brisbane City Council
description: A big bushland reserve in Brisbane's south, with sandstone boulders tucked under the canopy. Brisbane City Council recognised bouldering in three designated areas in June 2025, with signage and access sorted there. Bouldering is only allowed in those areas for now, so please stick to them. We're working with council towards opening more of the forest, and the guidebook is next.

name: White Rock
subtitle: Redbank Plains · Ipswich
councilStatus: Master plan allows bouldering in about half the area
description: Sandstone bouldering spread through the White Rock conservation area just south of Ipswich, and one of South East Queensland's biggest areas with very little written down. Ipswich City Council's master plan allows bouldering across about half of it. The track work is done, photos for the guide are being redone, and we're waiting to hear whether QPWS will take over managing access.

name: Plunketts
subtitle: Yarrabilba · Logan
councilStatus: QPWS are on board, talking with neighbours next
description: Sandstone boulders in Plunkett Conservation Park near Yarrabilba. The park is in Logan but managed by QPWS, who are happy for us to go ahead with mapping. Parts of the park back onto private land with no fence line, so stay within the park and keep off neighbouring properties. Mapping is about halfway done, and talking with the neighbours is next.

name: Cedar Creek
subtitle: Cedar Creek · Moreton Bay
councilStatus: Council is working through a plan for the area
description: Granite boulders along Cedar Creek, in rainforest north of Brisbane. The creek is a popular swimming spot and can flood after heavy rain, so check conditions before you go, and keep off the private properties near the end of Cedar Creek Road. Moreton Bay City Council is working through a plan for the area. We've mapped the tracks and boulders and are part way through the photos.

name: Passchendaele
subtitle: Stanthorpe · Southern Downs
description: Granite boulders spread through Passchendaele State Forest near Stanthorpe, with hundreds of problems under the trees. It's a working plantation managed by HQ Plantations, so access can close during harvesting: follow any signs and instructions from plantation staff, and there's no camping. HQ Plantations have been really supportive, and we're planning to meet them on site to go through the plan.
